concept: Conditional aggregation computes multiple metrics in one GROUP BY using CASE inside aggregate functions.
example:
SELECT CustomerID,
       SUM(CASE WHEN Amount >= 500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS LargeOrderCount,
       SUM(CASE WHEN Amount >= 500 THEN Amount ELSE 0 END) AS LargeOrderRevenue,
       COUNT(*) AS TotalOrders
FROM Orders
GROUP BY CustomerID;
breakdown: CASE produces a 1 or 0 for each order.
SUM of those flags counts orders matching the condition.
A second CASE sums only qualifying revenue.
GROUP BY returns one result row per customer.
practice: Add SmallOrderRevenue for orders below 500 and compute TotalRevenue.
answer:
SELECT CustomerID,
       SUM(CASE WHEN Amount < 500 THEN Amount ELSE 0 END) AS SmallOrderRevenue,
       SUM(Amount) AS TotalRevenue
FROM Orders
GROUP BY CustomerID;
takeaways: Use ELSE 0 when a zero contribution is intended.
COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(column) counts non-NULL values.
